analysis.title: Global Technology: Semiconductors - Memory: Strong 2027, A More Measured 2028: What is priced in, and what is the potential downside from AI capex cuts, LTA defaults, and memory price declines?
key_insights: GS keeps a constructive view on 2027 memory fundamentals but is more measured on 2028 due to AI capex sustainability concerns, weak smartphone/PC memory demand and higher China supply.
Current prices of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix appear to price in zero AI capex growth in 2028E plus an additional 40% ASP decline versus the GS base case.

LTA default risk looks limited: conventional DRAM prices would need to fall more than 32-54% below base case before customers have an economic incentive to default, and even with defaults revenue would only be 3-10% below a fully honored LTA scenario.

Under a 50% yoy DRAM and NAND ASP decline in 2028E (similar to 2019 and 2023 downcycles), SEC 2028E revenue/OP/NP would be 29%/54%/48% below base case, and SEC would still have a 35% OPM and trade at 4.7x P/E and 1.0x P/B.

DRAM S/D revised to undersupply of 4.1%/5.1%/1.2% for 2026E/2027E/2028E (from 5.0%/5.9%/3.9%). 2027 is expected to be the most severe shortage in 15+ years, while 2028 loosens on China supply and weaker phone/PC demand.
Conventional DRAM pricing forecast cut to +32%/-19% yoy for 2027E/2028E (from +32%/-5%). 2028E Hynix conventional DRAM ASP is US$1.76/Gb (from US$2.05).
NAND pricing forecast lowered to +20%/-21% yoy for 2027E/2028E (from +30%/-14%). NAND S/D moves to near balance in 2028E at 0.3% undersupply.
HBM TAM raised to US$60bn/US$200bn/US$237bn for 2026E/2027E/2028E on ASIC demand and higher ASPs. 2028E growth slows to 18% and memory optimization and datacenter delays are key 2028 downside risks.

HBM ASP is expected to return to a premium over conventional DRAM in 2027E (HBM ASP +100% yoy vs conventional ~+30%). HBM and conventional DRAM margins converge, which should keep conventional supply growth in check.

SEC is expected to gain HBM share (43% in 2027E/2028E) on ASIC and Nvidia exposure, with CXMT modeled at 5-6% share from 2027E. SEC HBM capacity is forecast at 280K/month by end-2027 and 310K/month by end-2028.

Hyperscaler capex is estimated at ~US$1.1tn in 2027E and US$1.2-1.3tn in 2028E, with memory ~40% of 2028E capex (from ~44% in 2027E). Flat/-10%/-20% capex in 2028 would cut memory spend by US$55bn/US$99bn/US$144bn.
Historically memory stocks bottom a few quarters, sometimes up to a year, before the earnings trough, so earnings cuts may already be discounted.
SEC TP cut to W350K (from W500K), Buy on APAC CL, with 2028E OP cut 26% and EPS cut 17%. Shareholder return yields are estimated at 17%/19% for 2027E/2028E.

Hynix TP cut to W2,000,000 (from W3,500,000), Buy, after moving to an average of P/E and P/B methodology and lowering target P/E to 5x from 7x. 2028E OP cut 23%, shareholder return yield 20%/22% for 2027E/2028E.

market_movers.rationale: TP cut from W500K on lower 2028E pricing and earnings. GS sees meaningful downside already priced in and a ~17-19% shareholder return yield. Buy is on the APAC Conviction List.
Samsung Electronics preference share TP cut from W380,000, using a 22% pref-to-common discount (from 24%).
SK Hynix TP cut from W3.5mn on lower target P/E and the addition of a P/B component. GS cites solid fundamentals and a ~20% shareholder return yield.

sector_views.rationale: 2027 DRAM and HBM undersupply is expected to persist and the stocks already price in severe 2028 downside, though 2028 forecasts are cut.

earnings_insights: SEC FY28E estimates (GS forecast) cut: sales W934.9tn (-16.6%), OP W508.7tn (-25.9%), net profit W442.3tn (-24.2%), EPS W75,325 (-16.7%). FY27E OP W574.5tn (-8.6%), EPS W75,076 (-4.9%).
Hynix FY28E estimates (GS forecast) cut: revenue W530.2tn (-18.6%), OP W380.1tn (-22.5%), EPS W537,899 (-21.6%). FY27E OP W428.2tn (-7.1%), EPS W546,421 (-6.8%). 4Q26E and FY26E are unchanged.
GS expects SEC 2028E OP to fall 11% yoy and EPS to stay flattish on buybacks. Hynix 2028E OP is also expected down 11% yoy and EPS down 2%.
Under the 50% ASP decline scenario Hynix 2028E revenue/OP/NP would be 39%/55%/52% below GS base case, at W322tn/W172tn/W146tn.
Estimates follow 3Q26 earnings. Base case SEC 2028E DRAM ASP -18% yoy and NAND ASP -21% yoy.

trade_ideas.description: Long Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix (Buy rated), as current prices already discount zero 2028 AI capex growth and a further 40% ASP decline
trade_ideas.rationale: Valuations of 2.0-2.4x 2028E P/E, a ~20% shareholder return yield and LTA protection limit downside.
trade_ideas.risk: Memory optimization, datacenter delays, AI capex cuts, major S/D deterioration.

risk_factors: Memory optimization by customers given rising cost burden.
AI capex cuts reducing HBM and overall memory demand.
Higher supply from China, mainly CXMT.
Weaker smartphone and PC demand as memory cost rises.
Major deterioration in memory S/D and delay in technology migration.
Sharp contraction in smartphone margins and mobile OLED share loss (SEC).
charts_described: Exhibits 28-29 show SEC and Hynix OP downside and implied value across flat/-10%/-20% 2028 AI capex and 20%/30%/40% additional ASP declines. The 40% ASP decline with flat capex implies roughly 0% upside for SEC (W183,000 implied value) and -3% for Hynix (W1,077,000).
Exhibits 48-49 plot SK Hynix 2017-2019 and SEC 2021-2023 share prices against quarterly OP, showing share price troughs ahead of the earnings trough.
vol_and_positioning: Memory stocks have corrected substantially over the past few months. SEC at W183,100 versus W262,000 on 8 Oct, and Hynix at W1,113,000 versus W2,333,000 on 31 May, so downside is argued to be largely priced in.
geopolitical: Higher China memory supply (CXMT) is a key driver of the 2028 outlook cut. GS models CXMT DRAM bit growth of 48%/36%/32% in 2026E/2027E/2028E and CXMT HBM supply from 2027E.

tension_points.bull_case: Shares already price in zero 2028 AI capex growth and an extra 40% ASP decline. LTAs protect revenue, and memory stocks historically bottom before earnings troughs.
tension_points.bear_case: AI capex sustainability concerns, memory optimization, datacenter delays, China supply and weak phone/PC demand could drive larger 2028 price declines. GS cut 2028E OP 23-26%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 2028 AI capex cut deeper than -20% yoy or ASP declines beyond an additional 40% versus base case, which would push implied value below current prices.

theme_stances.key_argument: Current SEC and Hynix prices already discount zero 2028 AI capex growth and a further 40% ASP decline.
theme_stances.evidence: meaningful downside risks have likely been priced in

theme_stances.key_argument: DRAM prices would need to fall 32-54% below base case before defaults, and defaults would only modestly reduce revenue.
